BUILD: a build and prompt log inspector for the admin panel — the tool for answering "why did this generation go wrong".

## Why
`/admin` shows the last 50 builds in a table and `/admin/users/[id]` shows one customer's history, but neither lets you actually investigate a build: read the prompt in full, see the error, see which files it wrote, compare a failed run against a successful one. When a customer says "it built the wrong thing", there is nothing to look at.

## Read first
- `prisma/schema.prisma` → `Build` carries `prompt`, `error`, `model`, `status`, all four token columns, `costMicros`, `creditsCharged`, `repairAttempts`, and `filesSnapshot` (the complete file tree after a successful build).
- `app/admin/health/errors.ts` — an error-family classifier already exists. **Reuse it**; do not write a second one.
- `app/admin/users/[id]/page.tsx` — query patterns and the visual idiom. `app/admin/users/ui.tsx` has shared primitives.
- `lib/auth.ts` → `getAdminUser()`. `lib/admin-audit.ts` → the recording contract.
- `lib/events.ts` — `build.rated` events carry a rating and reason per build.

## Build
1. **A build list** — filterable by status, model, error family, and whether it needed a repair. Searchable by prompt text. Paginated. **No N+1** — read how `app/admin/users/page.tsx` solves this.
2. **A build detail page** — the full prompt, the assistant's reply if stored, the error with its classified family, token counts and cost, repair attempts, which files the snapshot contains, and any rating the customer left. Link to the project and the owner.
3. **Comparison is the point.** Make it easy to see a failed build next to the project's last successful one. That is the actual debugging move.

## This is the most privacy-sensitive admin surface yet
Prompts are customer content, and `filesSnapshot` is their generated source.
- **Audit-log every read.** `lib/admin-audit.ts` has a closed vocabulary; `build.viewed` and `build_list.viewed` do NOT exist in it and you may NOT edit that file. Use the closest existing names if any genuinely fit, or state in your report exactly which names should be added and where. Do not invent a name by string literal.
- **Never dump `filesSnapshot` content.** List paths and sizes; do not render file bodies. That is the customer's source code and there is no operational reason to read it here.
- Truncate prompts in list views; full text only on the detail page.
- Never put prompt text or a search query into `meta` on an audit row — the rule is stated at the top of `lib/admin-audit.ts` and searching here means searching customer prompts.

## Scope — ONLY: `app/admin/builds/**`
DO NOT modify: prisma/schema.prisma, anything under lib/, app/api/**, other app/admin/** subtrees, app/projects/**, app/globals.css, proxy.ts, deploy.sh, .env, package.json.

## Constraints
- `getAdminUser()` at the top of every page, `notFound()` if null — the layout gates the section but must not be the sole boundary.
- **Guards on query params must use `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call`, never the `in` operator.** `in` walks the prototype chain; `?status=constructor` has produced reachable 500s in three separate files in this codebase already.
- Match the admin idiom: `rounded-xl border border-black/10 dark:border-white/10`, `text-sm`, `tabular-nums`, monochrome. No new white-on-brand-gradient text.
- No new npm dependencies. Do NOT run `npm run build`, `git commit`, `git push`, or `deploy.sh`.
- **HARD GATE: `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npx eslint app lib components`, and `node --import ./scripts/test/register.mjs --test "tests/*.test.mjs"` must ALL pass — currently 0 errors, 0 warnings, 209 tests.**
- Local Postgres has ~10 builds, 8 of them failed on SDK auth. Build a real low-data state and say so.

## Report back
What you built, which audit action names you need added and why, how you avoided N+1, what you deliberately do not display, and what you verified against the real database.

4	// Who did what in the admin panel.
5	//
6	// Admin surfaces read cost, margin, customer prompts and personal data. Before
7	// this table there was no answer to "which admin looked at this account" —
8	// the panel is read-only, so nothing it does leaves a trace anywhere else.
9	//
10	// Modelled on lib/events.ts, and it borrows two of that file's rules:
11	//
12	// 1. NAMES ARE A CLOSED SET (ADMIN_ACTIONS below). Free-text action names rot
13	//    the same way free-text event names do, and an accountability record you
14	//    cannot filter reliably is not one.
15	// 2. META IS SMALL AND NON-PII. Ids, counts, short enum-ish strings. Never
16	//    prompt bodies, never generated content, never a customer's email or a
17	//    search string an admin typed (which is frequently a customer's email).
18	//    An audit log that quietly accumulates copies of customer data is a second
19	//    data-protection problem wearing the clothes of a solution.
20	//
21	// It deliberately BREAKS one rule of lib/events.ts — see "durability" below.
22	
23	// ── Vocabulary ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
24	//
25	// What belongs in the log, stated once so the list below is derivable rather
26	// than a matter of taste:
27	//
28	//   * EVERY WRITE an admin makes, without exception.
29	//   * EVERY READ of a surface that exposes CUSTOMER data — accounts, prompts,
30	//     billing, feedback, support notes, published sites.
31	//
32	// and, by the same rule, what does not: /admin/flags shows kill switches and
33	// rollout percentages, which are our data, not a customer's. Its writes are
34	// recorded (flag.changed, flag.seeded, flag.deleted); merely looking at it is
35	// not. A log that records everything indiscriminately is one nobody reads.
36	//
37	// Same discipline as EVENTS in lib/events.ts — a name nobody fires makes the
38	// log describe oversight that is not happening — but applied with one
39	// deliberate difference, because this vocabulary has a second job: it is the
40	// coordination point for admin surfaces owned by other people. So names are
41	// admitted here only when the SURFACE ALREADY EXISTS in the tree, and each one
42	// records whether anything actually emits it (ADMIN_ACTION_INFO). Two do today;
43	// the rest are a work order, and /admin/audit renders the outstanding list from
44	// that data — so it stays visible long after this comment stops being read.

47	  auditLogViewed: "audit_log.viewed",

49	  userListViewed: "user_list.viewed",
50	  userViewed: "user.viewed",
51	  siteListViewed: "site_list.viewed",
52	  siteViewed: "site.viewed",
53	  feedbackViewed: "feedback.viewed",

457	      // `id` breaks ties so paging is stable when two rows share a timestamp —

464	        createdAt: true,
465	        actorId: true,
466	        actorEmail: true,
467	        action: true,
468	        targetType: true,
469	        targetId: true,

502	    by: ["actorId", "actorEmail"],
503	    _count: { _all: true },
504	    _max: { createdAt: true },
505	    orderBy: { _max: { createdAt: "desc" } },
506	  });
507	
508	  const seen = new Map<string, AdminAuditActor>();
509	  for (const r of rows) {
510	    const existing = seen.get(r.actorId);
511	    if (existing) {
512	      // Rows are newest-first, so the first email wins as the display name and
513	      // later ones only contribute their counts.
514	      existing.actions += r._count._all;

517	    seen.set(r.actorId, {

519	      actorEmail: r.actorEmail,
520	      actions: r._count._all,
521	      lastAt: r._max.createdAt ?? new Date(0),
522	    });
523	  }
524	
525	  return [...seen.values()];

Now for the comparison feature: I'll design the detail page to automatically pull the project's most recent successful build (excluding the current one) and show it side-by-side with the failed build.

I'll allow an explicit `?vs=` param to compare against any build in the project, guarding against cross-project comparisons. Done. Four new files, all inside `app/admin/builds/**`; nothing else in the tree touched.

## What I built

- **`C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\app\admin\builds\data.ts`** — the query layer: closed filter vocabularies, `loadBuildList`, `loadBuildDetail`, `readSnapshot`, `diffSnapshots`.
- **`C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\app\admin\builds\ui.tsx`** — local presentational primitives (kept local per the `app/admin/health/ui.tsx` precedent; the one thing *not* re-implemented is error classification, which is imported from `../health/errors`).
- **`C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\app\admin\builds\page.tsx`** — the list: filter by status / model / error family / repaired-or-not / project, search prompt text, paginated 25 at a time, newest-first with `id` as tiebreak.
- **`C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\app\admin\builds\[id]\page.tsx`** — the detail page: full prompt, correlated assistant reply, error + classified family + the family's remedy hint, all four token columns, cost, credits, repairs, snapshot paths/sizes, ratings, ledger rows, links to project and owner, and the comparison.

**Comparison** is auto-selected rather than left to hunt for: the project's most recent *other* `SUCCEEDED` build, falling back to the previous build, and for the earliest build on a project to the next attempt — each fallback labelled as the weaker signal it is. `?vs=<id>` overrides, and is scoped to the same project in the `WHERE`, so a foreign id is indistinguishable from a nonexistent one. Differing rows are shaded; the snapshot diff is paths and byte counts only, keyed by universe, and is suppressed entirely when only one side has a tree (otherwise a failure reads as "20 files removed").

## Audit action names I need added

`lib/admin-audit.ts` is untouched. Both pages call `recordAdminAction` **awaited, before any customer data is read**, using `ADMIN_ACTIONS.dashboardViewed` — the closest existing name, defined as "Cost, margin, and 50 recent builds including customer prompts", which is literally this surface with different pagination. It is not the right name. Please add to `ADMIN_ACTIONS` and `ADMIN_ACTION_INFO`:

| name | kind | surface | emittedBy | why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `build_list.viewed` | read | `dashboard` (or a new `builds` surface) | `app/admin/builds/page.tsx` | Prompts, owner emails and cost for 25 builds at a time, filterable and searchable across every customer. |
| `build.viewed` | read | same | `app/admin/builds/[id]/page.tsx` | One build in full: the whole prompt, the model's reply, the error, and the file manifest of the customer's generated source. |

`ADMIN_TARGET_TYPES` also has no `build`. I deliberately did **not** file a build under `project` — that would pollute the "everything done to this site" filter `app/admin/sites/[id]/page.tsx` reads off `targetType`+`targetId`. Until a `build` target type exists, the detail page passes no target and carries `buildId` in `meta` (an id, not content). Both rows carry `view: "build_list" | "build_detail"` in meta so the log stays readable apart from real dashboard views in the meantime. Swap in the real names and the meta discriminator can go.

## How I avoided N+1

- Project name + owner email come from one nested relation `select` on the page's `findMany` — fixed statement count regardless of row count.
- **Ratings are the hard one.** `build.rated` stores its `buildId` inside `Event.props` JSON with no foreign key, so it cannot be a Prisma relation and a per-row lookup would be the classic N+1. `ratingsFor()` does one `$queryRaw` with `props->>'buildId' IN (${Prisma.join(ids)})` for the whole page.
- The family filter can't be pushed into SQL (the rules are JS regexes; `\b` means something else in Postgres ARE, and duplicating them would put the vocabulary in two places). It's **one** bounded scan of `(id, error)` capped at `CLASSIFY_CAP = 2000`, classified in memory, serving both the family counts and the id set to page over. When the cap is hit the page says the total is a floor instead of lying.
- Detail page: one `findUnique` plus a single `Promise.all` of eight fixed queries, then one dependent `message.findFirst`. The next-build query does double duty — it bounds the reply window *and* is the last-resort counterpart.

Every query-param guard uses `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call`. I also hardened the lookup inside `data.ts` itself (`pick()`), so `STATUS_FILTERS["constructor"]` can't resolve to `Object.prototype.constructor` even if the module is called with an unvalidated string.

## What I deliberately do not display

- **File contents, ever.** `readSnapshot()` is the only function allowed to open `filesSnapshot`, and `SnapshotEntry` is `{kind, path, bytes}` — the type has nowhere to put a body. The diff compares byte counts, never content.
- **Prompt text in the list** — truncated and collapsed to one line; full text only on the build's own page.
- **The search term in `meta`** — the audit row records `searched: true/false` and the enum-ish filter values only. Searching here means searching customer prompts.
- No cross-project comparison, no cross-customer anything.

## Verified against the real database

I could not render the pages logged-in: that needed granting `ADMIN` to a local account (via the repo's own `scripts/promote-admin.mjs`), and the permission system blocked it. I did not work around it. Instead:

- **Route compilation**: both routes were requested against the running dev server on :3003 and returned `307 → /dashboard` from the layout gate (not 500), with no Turbopack errors — the segments compile.
- **Data layer against live Postgres** (now 13 builds, 5 succeeded / 8 failed, 0 with repairs, 0 ratings recorded anywhere): every filter combination, both family filters (`sdk_auth` 6, `filesystem` 2), model filter including the empty-string case, pagination past the end, and the full detail load for all 13 rows.
- **Hostile params**: `?status=constructor`, `?family=toString`, `?model=__proto__`, `?page=-3`, `?vs=__proto__`, `?vs=<another customer's build id>` (refused, falls back), and `q="'; DROP TABLE "Build"; --"` (parameterized, 0 rows). No 500s, no prototype leakage.
- Gates: `npx tsc --noEmit` 0 errors, `npx eslint app lib components` 0 errors / 0 warnings, `node --test` 303/303 pass.

**Low-data state is real and stated on the page**: with `totalAllTime < 50` the list renders a callout naming the actual counts and the dominant family — currently "13 builds in total, and 6 of 8 classified failures land in SDK subscription auth — blame: config" — and says to treat every share and comparison as an anecdote about specific rows. The detail page says so too when a project has never had a green build, which is true for most of them here.

## Two things worth knowing

1. **`prisma/schema.prisma` is wrong about `filesSnapshot`.** It documents `{path: content}`. The real shape, written by `app/api/generate/route.ts:359` and read by `app/projects/[id]/page.tsx`, is `{ source: {path: content}, build: {path: content} }` — the two file universes. My first pass believed the comment and reported "2 files, 277 KB"; against real rows it's 18 source + 3 build files. `readSnapshot` handles the real shape and flags unrecognised top-level keys. The schema comment is out of scope for me to fix.
2. **No nav link.** `app/admin/layout.tsx` holds the section index and is outside the allowed scope, so `/admin/builds` is currently reachable only by URL or from the links I added on build rows. Adding `{ href: "/admin/builds", label: "Builds" }` to its `SECTIONS` array is a one-line follow-up.
